subject: Post-call recap: inference cost pressure & qualification
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Barnes <luke@finopsco.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finopsco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: inference cost pressure & qualification

Thanks for taking time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. High level notes from our call: 

- Pain: token spend growing fast (>3x last 6 months) and finance flagged unit economics as a hard stop for Q4 expansion. Current estimated per-1k-token cost (infra + licensing) ~ $0.42 and margins are under pressure.
- Current stack: in-house endpoint on GCP using a mix of FP16 models with naive batching; no KV/prefix caching in front of the model; retriever + reranker pipeline that sends ~40% of requests to the LLM.
- Perf targets: p95 generation latency goal <= 400ms for customer-facing completions; peak concurrent QPS observed ~110 requests/sec during spikes.
- Ops constraints: unable to run aggressive batching today due to latency spikes and brittle autoscaling; team is open to model quantization but needs proof of negligible quality regressions for 95% of prompts.

Success criteria we discussed (to qualify a pilot):
1) Demonstrable unit-cost reduction >= 35% at production scale while keeping p95 latency <= 450ms.
2) No more than a 3% drop in key NLU/QA accuracy metrics on a small evaluation set you share.
3) Clear plan for rollout: canary -> 20% -> 100% with automated fallback.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
- FinOpsCo: share token profile CSV (bucketed by route/intent), peak TPS by hour, and 2–3 representative prompt sets for A/B quality checks (you said Priya can share).
- Redwood: we will run a quick cost sensitivity model (sheet attached: cost_model_v1.xlsx) and a short quantization impact test (using your prompt set) and deliver an initial pilot hypothesis within 5 business days.
- Align on a pilot scope call: Wed Jul 28 10:00 PT — Karthik will join to cover batching/caching options and quantization tradeoffs.

Attachments: finopsco_token_profile.csv (sample expected format), cost_model_v1.xlsx (Redwood cost sensitivity workbook), redwood_quantization_factsheet.pdf

If this looks right, reply with the token CSV and confirm Wed 28 10:00 PT.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai

Thanks Vanessa — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications before we send the CSV: 

1) Token profile: we'll provide 14 days of anonymized traffic with intent labels (support, search, recommendations). Expect the file by EOD today (Priya is looping in).
2) Latency tolerance: 450ms p95 is acceptable for support/search; recommendations can tolerate up to 750ms p95.
3) Quality gates: we can give you a 500-sample eval with baseline metrics (F1/EM for QA, relevance NDCG for recommendations).

Agree to Wed 28 10:00 PT pilot scope call. We'll include our infra lead on the call if we have them available.

Luke

Appreciate the quick turn, Priya — received the CSV and prompt set (thanks). Follow-up notes and actions from Redwood: 

- Karthik will run a microbenchmark this week to estimate achievable batching levels with p95 <= 450ms and produce a recommended batching configuration (batch sizes, max latency budget, continuous batching window parameters).
- We'll run quantization tests (INT8 / FP16 compare) on the 500-sample eval and report any regressions; the redwood_quantization_factsheet.pdf outlines expected quality/latency tradeoffs.
- Cost model: updated cost_model_v1.xlsx will include a reserved vs PAYG comparison and sensitivity to model size and QPS. Expect the first pass by Tue Aug 2 EOD.
- Pilot proposal: 4-week canary scoped to the support and search routes (these are higher volume and tighter latency). If metrics look good, expand to recommendations in week 5.

Questions for you both before the pilot:
1) Do you have a preferred SLA template or procurement constraints we should be aware of?
2) Are there internal test accounts we can use for canary traffic that won't affect production billing?

I'll send calendar invite for Wed Jul 28 10:00 PT and include Karthik. Any objections, please flag.

Thanks — looking forward.
